intro: Stirling is genuinely a small city with an outsized place in Scottish history, its strategic position controlling the lowest crossing point of the River Forth making it central to centuries of conflict.

Its castle, genuinely one of Scotland's grandest, overlooks the plain where William Wallace and Robert the Bruce both won decisive battles for Scottish independence, at Stirling Bridge in 1297 and Bannockburn in 1314.
Most visitors genuinely visit as a day trip from Glasgow or Edinburgh, though an overnight allows time to properly cover the castle, the Wallace Monument and the battlefields without rushing.

attractionsIntro: Stirling's essential sights combine a genuinely grand royal castle with the battlefields that shaped Scottish independence.

attractions.name: Stirling Castle
attractions.text: Genuinely one of Scotland's grandest castles, a former royal residence with sweeping views over the surrounding plain.
attractions.tip: Genuinely allow at least half a day — the castle's grounds and interiors are more extensive than they first appear.

attractions.name: The Royal Palace at Stirling Castle

image.alt: The Royal Palace within Stirling Castle

attractions.text: Genuinely meticulously restored royal apartments, recreating the castle's Renaissance-era grandeur with real historical accuracy.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the recreated tapestries and painted ceilings are a highlight, based on real historical research.

attractions.name: The Wallace Monument
attractions.text: Genuinely a dramatic Victorian tower honouring William Wallace, with 246 steps leading to sweeping views from the top.
attractions.tip: Genuinely check the crown steeple viewing platform's opening hours before making the climb.

attractions.name: The Great Hall

image.alt: The Great Hall at Stirling Castle

attractions.text: Genuinely the largest medieval banqueting hall ever built in Scotland, restored to its original lime-washed golden exterior.
attractions.tip: Genuinely check for occasional historical re-enactment events held inside the hall.

attractions.name: Old Stirling Bridge

image.alt: Old Stirling Bridge over the River Forth

attractions.text: Genuinely near the site of William Wallace's decisive 1297 victory, though the current stone bridge dates from later centuries.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a pleasant, easy walk along the River Forth from the city centre.

attractions.name: Bannockburn

image.file: File:Robert the Bruce statue and Bannockburn memorial - geograph.org.uk - 4017818.jpg
image.alt: The Bannockburn battlefield memorial near Stirling

attractions.text: Genuinely the site of Robert the Bruce's decisive 1314 victory over England, central to winning Scottish independence.
attractions.tip: The genuinely visitor centre's interactive battle experience adds real context to the open battlefield site.

attractions.name: Stirling Old Town Jail

image.alt: The Old Town Jail in Stirling

attractions.text: Genuinely a well-preserved Victorian prison, its history illustrating the harsh realities of 19th-century justice.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a short walk from Stirling Castle, easy to combine in the same visit.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Stirling Castle's Royal Palace

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding, if strenuous, climb of 246 spiral steps to sweeping views from the crown steeple.

thingsToDo.title: Learn Bruce's history at Bannockburn

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely engaging visitor centre experience, bringing the 1314 battle to life through interactive exhibits.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book ahead for the 3D battle experience, which runs on a timed-entry basis.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Old Town Jail

image.alt: The Old Town Jail building in Stirling

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely engaging hour exploring 19th-century prison life, with costumed guides throughout.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine easily with a Stirling Castle visit, given the short walk between them.

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely free, sweeping view over the city and surrounding plain, no ticket required.
